scenes.text: The first jack-o'-lanterns weren't pumpkins. They were turnips.
In Ireland and Scotland, people carved creepy faces into turnips and other root vegetables.
In parts of England, they used large beets instead.
The name comes from an Irish folktale about a trickster called Stingy Jack, doomed to wander with a lantern.
When Irish, Scottish and English immigrants reached America, they found pumpkins, which are much easier to carve.
Old turnip lanterns look way scarier than pumpkins.
Would you carve a turnip this Halloween?

title: The first jack-o'-lanterns were turnips, not pumpkins 🎃
caption: Before pumpkins, people in Ireland and Scotland carved jack-o'-lanterns from turnips, and in England from beets. Immigrants brought the tradition to America, where pumpkins took over. 🎃
